q.t: How many halves make one whole?
q.e: Sharing a whole equally between 2 people gives 2 equal parts, and each part is a half.

q.t: How many quarters make one whole?
q.e: Sharing a whole equally among 4 people gives 4 equal parts, and each is a quarter.

q.t: What is half of 8 marbles?
q.e: Split 8 into 2 equal groups: 4 and 4.

q.t: What is double of 5 marbles?
q.e: Double means two times as many: 5 + 5 = 10.

q.t: A whole is shared equally among 4 people. Each share is called:
q.e: One of 4 equal parts of a whole is a quarter.

q.t: A whole is shared equally between 2 people. Each share is called:
q.e: One of 2 equal parts of a whole is a half.

q.t: What is half of 12 marbles?
q.e: 6 + 6 = 12, so half of 12 is 6.

q.t: What is double of 6 marbles?
A paratha is cut into two pieces, one big and one small. Is each piece a half?
o: Yes, any two pieces are halves
Yes, if the paratha is round
Only the bigger piece is a half
q.e: A half is a fair share: both parts must be exactly the same size.

q.t: 2 quarters of a chikki make:
q.e: 4 quarters make a whole, so 2 quarters are half of the whole.

q.t: Peehu ties a quarter of her 16 flowers. How many flowers does she tie?
q.e: A quarter means 4 equal groups: 16 shared into 4 is 4 each.

q.t: Lakshanya ties half of her 16 flowers. How many does she tie?
q.e: 16 split into 2 equal groups is 8 and 8.

q.t: 3 quarters and 1 more quarter make:
q.e: 3 + 1 = 4 quarters, and 4 quarters make one whole.

q.t: What is half of 14?
What is double of 9?
3 marbles is half of how many marbles?
q.e: If 3 is half, the whole is double of 3: 3 + 3 = 6.

q.t: How many halves are there in 3 wholes?
q.e: Each whole has 2 halves: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6.

q.t: How many quarters are there in 2 wholes?
q.e: Each whole has 4 quarters: 4 + 4 = 8.

q.t: Which is bigger: half of a chikki or a quarter of the same chikki?
q.e: Sharing among 2 gives bigger pieces than sharing among 4.

q.t: Amit keeps all the mangoes and gives Bala only the tree. Is that a fair share?
o: No, Bala gets nothing to eat
q.e: Fair sharing means both get an equal amount of what is useful — Bala never gets any fruit.

q.t: What is a quarter of 20 laddoos?
q.e: 20 shared into 4 equal groups: 5 in each, because 4 × 5 = 20.

q.t: What is three quarters of 8 marbles?
q.e: One quarter of 8 is 2, so three quarters is 2 + 2 + 2 = 6.

q.t: 4 marbles is half of how many marbles?
q.e: The whole is double the half: 4 + 4 = 8.

q.t: Riddle: I have fewer than double of 5 marbles and more than half of 16 marbles. How many do I have?
q.e: Double of 5 is 10 and half of 16 is 8. More than 8 but fewer than 10 means 9.

q.t: How many quarters make one half?
q.e: A whole is 4 quarters, and half of 4 quarters is 2 quarters.

q.t: Lakshanya ties half of 16 flowers; Peehu ties a quarter of 16. Lakshanya tied ___ the number Peehu tied.
q.e: Lakshanya tied 8 and Peehu tied 4, and 8 is double of 4.

q.t: What is three quarters of 12 birds?
q.e: A quarter of 12 is 3, so three quarters is 3 + 3 + 3 = 9.

q.t: A pizza is cut into 4 equal pieces and Ravi eats 1 piece. What part of the pizza is left?
q.e: 4 quarters − 1 quarter = 3 quarters.

q.t: Take half of 10, then double the answer. What do you get?
q.e: Half of 10 is 5, double of 5 is 10. Doubling undoes halving.

q.t: There are 12 birds. Shabnam colours 6 of them. What part of the birds did she colour?
q.e: 6 + 6 = 12, so 6 is half of 12.

q.t: Kavi has 24 marbles. He gives half to his sister. Then he gives a quarter of what is left to a friend. How many marbles does Kavi have now?
q.e: Half of 24 is 12, so 12 are left. A quarter of 12 is 3. 12 − 3 = 9.

q.t: Raj has 7 stickers. Mona has double the number Raj has. How many stickers do they have together?
q.e: Mona has 7 + 7 = 14. Together: 7 + 14 = 21.

q.t: Shabnam eats a quarter of a chikki, then another quarter. What part is left?
q.e: She ate 2 quarters, which is a half, so the other half is left.

q.t: There are 20 laddoos. Half go to Nani and a quarter of the 20 go to Mama. How many are left?
q.e: Half of 20 is 10 and a quarter of 20 is 5. 20 − 10 − 5 = 5.

q.t: Riddle: I am more than half of 14 and less than double of 5. Which of these can I be?
q.e: Half of 14 is 7 and double of 5 is 10. I must be bigger than 7 and smaller than 10 — only 8 fits.

q.t: 8 mangoes are shared equally between 2 children. One child then gives half of her share to a friend. How many mangoes does she keep?
q.e: Each child gets 4. Half of 4 is 2.

q.t: A ribbon is folded in half, and then folded in half again. When you open it, how many equal parts are there?
q.e: The first fold makes 2 halves; folding again halves each half: 4 quarters.

q.t: Which is the same as three quarters?
q.e: A half is 2 quarters, and 2 quarters + 1 quarter = 3 quarters.

q.t: Asha eats half a roti. Bina eats 2 quarters of a roti of the same size. Who eats more?
q.e: 2 quarters make exactly a half.

q.t: Start with 13. Double it, then take half of the answer. What do you get?
q.e: Double of 13 is 26 and half of 26 is 13. Halving undoes doubling.
